title: Encrypted DNS Provisioning RFC 9464 Exchange Planner Architecture
purpose: Define the local RFC 9464 Configuration Payload exchange planner that composes support advertisements, responder replies, and client resolver plans before live IKEv2 integration.
design_summary: The exchange planner models the RFC 9464 encrypted DNS attributes inside IKEv2 Configuration Payloads without implementing a live IKEv2 session. It validates that ENCDNS_IP* and ENCDNS_DIGEST_INFO attributes match their Configuration Payload type, creates CFG_REQUEST support advertisements with optional digest algorithm lists, creates CFG_REPLY payloads from responder policy, and creates client resolver plans from CFG_REPLY or CFG_SET payloads. `EncryptedDnsProvisioningTransportExecutor` exchanges CFG_REQUEST and CFG_REPLY payloads through an explicit transport adapter contract for deterministic fake-backed IKEv2 boundary proof.
data_and_state_considerations: The planner is side-effect free and immutable. The executor invokes only the caller-supplied transport adapter. These components consume existing codec, responder, and client policy types and produce value objects that a future IKEv2 adapter can serialize, receive, or map to platform APIs. They do not own packet exchange, IPsec state, host resolver mutation, or encrypted DNS session establishment.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A responder reply can only be planned from a CFG_REQUEST payload.
Payload attributes and digest information must match the modeled Configuration Payload type.
A discarded request produces an empty CFG_REPLY payload and no encrypted resolver endpoints.
Client resolver planning accepts only CFG_REPLY or CFG_SET payloads.
risks: Treating this planner or fake-backed transport proof as live IKEv2 support would overstate the implementation.
Skipping the local model would force each future IKEv2 or platform adapter to duplicate RFC 9464 request/reply validation.
Adding platform resolver behavior here would couple DNS value policy to operating-system integration.
